title: What can you say about potassium in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for potassium; the strongest is "A source of electrolytes" (moderate, 100-200 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Lowers blood pressure, or treats hypertension", and keep "Helps maintain normal blood pressure" off Meta ads.

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 100-200 mg a day; no other listed source covers this wording.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: at least 100 mg a day is needed for this use, below 100 mg only general wording applies, and the maximum is 200 mg a day. ODS: most US potassium supplements give at most 99 mg.
supported_wordings.form: Potassium from a salt on Health Canada's list (such as citrate, chloride or gluconate), counted as potassium

supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review; Health Canada does not list it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: at least 300 mg, 15% of the 2,000 mg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). Health Canada's multi-vitamin/mineral monograph allows at most 200 mg a day, below this threshold. ODS: no upper limit was set.
supported_wordings.form: Potassium from a salt on Health Canada's list (such as citrate, chloride or gluconate), counted as potassium

supported_wordings.meta_ads: Wording to avoid in Meta ads. On your site it is supported wording.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers blood pressure, or treats hypertension
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. FDA's 2000 rule (page 1006) counts a claim that a product promotes low blood pressure as a disease claim.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Reduces the risk of stroke or heart disease

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a medical condition. ODS says abnormal blood potassium levels are rare in healthy people with normal kidney function.
Blood pressure is a health-condition claim on Meta, so this wording stays off Meta ads (library decision of 2026-10-15; Meta's ad policies were not read). It is supported wording for pages.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
